summary.detailed_summary: BELT proposes a learning framework to translate noninvasive EEG signals into natural language by utilizing the semantic knowledge of off-the-shelf large language models. It employs a deep conformer encoder and a vector quantization encoder, using a contrastive learning objective to align EEG representations with natural language supervision. The model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in brain-to-language translation and zero-shot sentiment classification.
key_points: Uses a conformer and vector quantization encoder to align brain signals with natural language semantics.
Employs contrastive learning with pretrained LMs to overcome the limitation of small-scale EEG datasets.
Achieves state-of-the-art results in brain-to-language translation and zero-shot sentiment classification.
limitations: Dependence on the quality of the pretrained language model
Limited scale and quality of available EEG datasets for initial training

method.architecture: Deep conformer encoder and vector quantization (VQ) encoder
method.finetuning: Applied to translation and sentiment classification tasks
method.objective: Contrastive learning with natural language supervision

summary.one_liner: A framework that leverages pretrained language models via contrastive learning to bootstrap semantic EEG representations for brain-to-language translation.
summary.title: BELT:Bootstrapping Electroencephalography-to-Language Decoding and Zero-Shot Sentiment Classification by Natural Language Supervision
summary.unique_contribution: Bootstraps EEG representation learning by using contrastive alignment with large-scale pretrained language models to enable zero-shot semantic decoding.

reasons: EEG is the central modality focused on brain-to-language translation.
Proposes a generic framework to bootstrap EEG representation learning using large-scale pretrained language models.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization capabilities, a key characteristic of foundation models.
Aims to create semantically discriminative EEG representations for broad application across decoding tasks.
